---
title: "A user-supplied grammar"
format: html
---

TOML is not one of Quarto's built-in highlighting languages. This
project adds it by shipping a tree-sitter grammar in
`_quarto/grammars/toml/`: the compiled `toml.wasm` and its
`highlights.scm` query. Any code block marked `toml` now picks it up:

```toml
# Site configuration
[server]
host = "localhost"
port = 8080
debug = false
started = 2026-11-05T09:30:00Z

[[server.routes]]
path = "/docs"
cache = { enabled = true, max-age = 3600 }
```

Inline code works the same way: `retries = 3`{.toml}.

The grammar's capture names become CSS classes: a capture `@name.sub`
is emitted as `<span class="hl-name-sub">`. This grammar's query
captures TOML keys as `@type`, so the style block below sets `.hl-type`
in bold; the colors come from the default palette.

```{=html}
<style>
.hl-type { font-weight: 600; }
</style>
```
